A record is counted as VERIFIED only when the record contains: 1. a stable record identifier; 2. provenance/source information; 3. evidence or an evidence reference; 4. an explicit independent-verification object; 5. verification status exactly equal to `VERIFIED`; 6. a verification timestamp or run reference; and 7. a deterministic SHA-256 fingerprint of the canonical record payload. A scheduled/completed GitHub Actions run alone is never counted as a VERIFIED research record. ## Status model - `CANDIDATE` — discovered but not verified. - `REVIEW` — has evidence/provenance but lacks complete verification. - `VERIFIED` — satisfies every gate above. - `REJECTED` — explicitly rejected or fails a hard verification gate. ## Measurement The verifier publishes: - total candidate records; - VERIFIED records; - REVIEW records; - REJECTED records; - verification percentage; - remaining percentage; - target progress toward 100,200 VERIFIED records. The verifier is fail-closed: missing evidence, provenance, verification metadata, or fingerprint prevents a record from being counted as VERIFIED.
